example_summary: Analysis of asset transactions under Section 47 exempting gifts, HUF partition distributions, and debenture conversions from capital gains tax.
source_provision:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Section 47 Exclusions

| Statutory Section | Transaction Category | Statutory Condition / Trigger | Tax Treatment / Legal Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 47(iii)** | Gift, Will, or Irrevocable Trust | Transfer of a capital asset by an individual or HUF under a gift, will, or irrevocable trust | **Not Regarded as Transfer**: Capital gains tax liability does not arise |
| **Section 47(i)** | Partition of HUF | Transfer of a capital asset (in kind) on total or partial partition of a Hindu Undivided Family | **Not Regarded as Transfer**: Capital gains tax liability does not arise |
| **Section 47(x)** | Conversion of Debentures / Bonds | Conversion of bonds, debentures, or deposit certificates into shares or debentures of that company | **Not Regarded as Transfer**: Capital gains tax liability does not arise |


> [!IMPORTANT] Scope of Section 45(1): Charging Section
> Capital gains tax under Section 45(1) applies cumulatively only when there is a valid 'transfer' of a 'capital asset' resulting in 'profits or gains' during the relevant previous year.


> [!WARNING] Statutory Overrides
> Even if a transaction involves the extinguishment of rights or relinquishment of an asset, if it falls squarely within any clause of Section 47, it overrides the general definition of transfer under Section 2(47).

director.justification: The scenarios evaluate whether specific asset movements meet the statutory criteria under Section 47 to be excluded from the definition of 'transfer' for capital gains purposes.
director.visual_metaphor: A 'Safe Passage' corridor where specific transactions bypass the tax collector's booth because they are not recognized as transfers.

beat_plan.beat_goal: Introduce the three scenarios involving gold gifts, HUF partition, and debenture conversion.
Establish the legal foundation that Section 47 overrides the general charging section.
Analyze Scenario (i) regarding the gift of gold to a son.
Analyze Scenario (ii) regarding the distribution of property on HUF partition.
Analyze Scenario (iii) regarding the conversion of debentures into shares.
Conclude that no tax liability arises in any of the three cases.

beats.voice_sync_text: ഇവിടെ നമ്മൾ പഠിക്കുന്നത് capital gains chapter-ലെ വളരെ important ആയ ഒരു statutory concept ആണ്. Mr. A purchased gold for ₹ 25,000 and gifted it, HUF distributed property, and Mr. B converted debentures. We evaluate the Capital Gains Tax Liability in these scenarios.

visual_data.transaction: Evaluating Capital Gains Tax Liability for asset movements

beats.director_goal: Introduce the three scenarios involving gold gifts, HUF partition, and debenture conversion.

beats.voice_sync_text: Capital gains tax under Section 45(1) applies cumulatively only when there is a valid transfer. However, Section 47 lists transactions that are Not Regarded as Transfer for tax purposes.

visual_data.rule: Transactions listed under Section 47 override the charging provisions of Section 45(1).
visual_data.application: Not Regarded as Transfer: Specific asset movements bypass capital gains tax liability.

beats.director_goal: Establish the legal foundation that Section 47 overrides the general charging section.

beats.voice_sync_text: Section 47(iii) അനുസരിച്ച് ഒരു individual അല്ലെങ്കിൽ HUF തങ്ങളുടെ capital asset Gift ആയിട്ടോ will ആയിട്ടോ transfer ചെയ്യുമ്പോൾ അത് transfer ആയി കണക്കാക്കില്ല. Though FMV was ₹ 1,00,000, no capital gains arise.

beats.voice_sync_text: ഇനി Hindu Undivided Family-യുടെ total അല്ലെങ്കിൽ partial partition നടക്കുമ്പോൾ assets members-ലേക്ക് distribute ചെയ്യുന്നത് Section 47(i) പ്രകാരം transfer ആയി treat ചെയ്യുന്നതല്ല. Even with FMV of ₹ 12,00,000 on HUF Partition, tax is not levied.
